title: Fail on inapplicable flags on non-common commands expanded from configs

timeline.author: Fabian Meumertzheim

diff.patch:
@@ -282,6 +282,27 @@ def testCommonPseudoCommand_allowResidueFalseCommandIgnoresStarlarkOptions(
     # Check that version doesn't fail.
     self.RunBazel(["version"])
 
+  def testConfigExpansion_failsOnUnsupportedFlag(self):
+    self.ScratchFile("MODULE.bazel")
+    self.ScratchFile("BUILD.bazel")
+    self.ScratchFile(
+      ".bazelrc",
+      [
+        "build:abc --copt",
+        "build:abc -DFOO",
+        "common:abc --noverbose_test_summary",
+        "common:abc --verbose_test_summary",
+        "build:abc --copt",
+        "build:abc -DFOO",
+        "build:abc --verbose_test_summary",
+        "common:def --config=abc"
+      ],
+    )
+
+    exit_code, stdout, stderr = self.RunBazel(["build", "--announce_rc", "--config=def", "//..."], allow_failure=True)
+    self.AssertExitCode(exit_code, 2, stderr)
+    self.assertIn("ERROR: --verbose_test_summary :: Unrecognized option: --verbose_test_summary", stderr)
+
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
   absltest.main()

timeline.body: I can't use records in this target as it needs to be compatible with Java 11.

reply.body: I wasn't aware of any requirement to support java 11 still. Where are you seeing that?
Thanks, I asked around to confirm that it's still necessary, but I'll proceed with reviewing.

timeline.body: I don't think you can use `getFirst()` in this file given the java 11 thing.

reply.body:
This actually doesn't break CI since the bootclasspath is determined by the Java runtime version, not the language level. But it would break the consumers that legitimately build with a JDK 11, so good catch on your part.

@cushon @hvadehra Since this is coming up in Bazel code, what do you think of reinvigorating https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_java/pull/182?
I won't take credit, a breakage popped up when I imported.

timeline.body: Why do we need both this class and the one in `OptionsParserImpl`? Is it something to do with a dependency issue with `OpaqueOptionsData` and `OptionsData`? Seems like we could improve that situation.

reply.body: I thought it was, but by moving the cast into this class I found a way to avoid it and reduce the number of new classes from 3 to 1.
Excellent! There's probably still a way we can clean up the class hierarchy, but at least it's not making this change substantially messier now.
